text:
Either/Or · Game rules
The 16 players make 10 choices and play 4 minigames. Answer each choice on your own terminal. Choices and minigame results affect cumulative Victory Points. Everyone starts at 0 Victory Points, and any changes are made public. The default starting balance is 1 Piece.
By default, ranks 1–6 go to the Living Quarters, ranks 7–14 go to the Prison Wing, and the bottom 2 are eliminated. First place can use the Alliance Token to move one player from the Prison Wing to the Living Quarters.

Choice 1 · Bonus or Insurance
Bonus pays 1 Piece if you end up in the Living Quarters. Insurance pays 2 Pieces if you end up in the Prison Wing. Payouts are based on the final assignments after the Alliance Token is used.

Minigame 1 · Cube Counting
Count all cubes in the revealed stack and submit your answer through your terminal. Only you learn if your answer was correct. After a wrong answer, wait 20 seconds before trying again. Correct answers establish priority in submission order. The game ends once 15 players answer correctly, and the remaining player receives priority rank 16. Priority breaks ties on Victory Points or tile numbers in later stages.
In the simulation, each player's first submission time is set on a simulated clock. After a wrong answer, that player submits again 20 seconds later.

text:
Choice 2 · Team or Solo
Play Rectangle Counting solo or in a team of 3. A team is confirmed only when all 3 players submit the same lineup. Everyone else plays solo. Confirmed teams cannot change before Rectangle Counting ends.
Players can submit privately on their own turns at any point during negotiation. The teams are revealed and the game begins once everyone submits. At the deadline, collect a final choice from anyone who has not yet submitted.

Minigame 2 · Rectangle Counting
Count the rectangles on the revealed grid whose cells add up to the target. Blank cells count as 0. All rectangles must align with the grid. A single square or the whole board can qualify.
Each puzzle has a 5-minute limit. After buzzing in, you have 10 seconds to answer. In the simulation, submit only the answer. Buzzes are processed in the order responses arrive. A solo player or team that answers incorrectly may not retry the same puzzle. Move on when someone answers correctly, when time runs out without a correct answer, or when every entry has answered incorrectly.
A solo player or team that answers 2 puzzles correctly wins and sits out the remaining puzzles. Count each solo player and each team of 3 as one entry. Play ends when half the entries have won. Solo players gain 7 Victory Points for a win or lose 3 for a loss. A team of 3 shares 7 Victory Points for a win and loses 3 or 4 in total for a loss.

Choice 5 · Points or Information
Choose Points to gain 5 Victory Points. Choose Information to privately preview the options and detailed rules for Choices 6–8 before selecting a tile.
The broadcast allows 5 minutes to read the information preview and another 20 minutes before play begins. The simulation allows 10 negotiation rounds before Choice 5 and 10 after it. Players who receive the preview write one private plan before the second negotiation.

The 5 in Choice 5 is the stage number in Either/Or.
The available tile numbers are 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, and 13.
Players publicly choose one tile, starting with the lowest cumulative Victory Points. Multiple players may choose the same tile number. A choice cannot be changed.
Place tiles in ascending order of the numbers players chose. Break ties in either order using priority.
Tiles may be rotated in 90-degree increments. Flipping, overlapping tiles, and placements off the board are prohibited.
A successful placement normally earns Victory Points equal to the tile number. A failed placement earns 0. Final placement scores are settled after every player has taken a turn.

If pledges total at least 8, highest-ranked contributors pay up to their pledges in rank order until 8 Pieces are collected. If pledges total less than 8, nobody pays.

text:
Minigame 4 · Memory Poker and Choice 10
Starting ranks are based on Victory Points through Lay the Grass, with Cube Counting priority breaking ties. From here on, survival depends on ranks changed by poker duels. The points table shows standings before poker begins.
For each duel, show 16 cards drawn at random from a 52-card deck for 20 seconds, then reveal 3 community cards. The two players privately select 2 positions. Reveal both choices and compare each 5-card hand using the selected 2 cards and all 3 community cards. In the simulation, each player chooses 8–10 positions to memorize. They may guess unmemorized positions when submitting their final choices.
The hand rankings, from strongest to weakest, are straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, and high card. Break a tie within the same hand type by comparing the ranks of the cards forming the hand, then the remaining cards. Suits do not break ties. An ace can be low in an A–2–3–4–5 straight. If the hands are identical in rank, deal new cards and replay.
In Choice 10, Nomination applies with at least 8 votes and Ladder with at least 9. The players in 15th and 16th place start their streaks in that order. In Nomination, challengers pick a higher-ranked opponent they have not faced in that streak. On a win, the challenger moves up one place and the opponent moves down one. The simulation applies the challenger's upward swap, then the opponent's downward swap. If the opponent is immediately above, swap only once. If the opponent starts 2 places above, the two swaps move the challenger up 2. A successful defending player earns 1 Piece. In Ladder, a win against the player immediately above swaps their ranks.
A streak ends when the challenger loses or has no eligible opponent left. The player who newly falls to 15th or 16th becomes the next challenger. Players who have already been challenged do not return. The game ends when there is no new challenger.
